answer: At each dawn epoch, every agent must commit a unique Blake3 hash over its dedicated 64 GB RAM array, salted by the prior epoch’s state root, before any peer will accept its identity proofs. A verifier then samples 512 random offsets, requesting Merkle proofs against that locked root; honest agents answer instantly because the array never left memory, while a Sybil farm reusing one physical host cannot hold thousands of distinct 64 GB commitments, so its proofs collide or stall. Each probe is sealed with a horizon signature and logged in a nectar ledger.
